chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habeeb, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The water of the bathhouse is permissible (there is no problem with it) if it has a source (like a flowing spring or continuous supply).
ai.seo_question: Is the water in a bathhouse considered pure for ritual ablution?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the purity of bathhouse water, a common concern in early Islamic urban centers. The condition of having a 'source' (maddah) distinguishes flowing or replenished water from stagnant pools, aligning with the Shia juristic principle that water remains pure unless its essence changes due to impurity. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility of Shia fiqh in accommodating daily hygiene practices while maintaining ritual purity standards.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Bakr Bin Habeeb, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The water of the bathhouse, there is no problem with it, if there was a source for it (like a fountain)’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Bakr ibn Habib who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Water of bathhouses does not have problems if it is water from a large source; like a fountain.’”
